description: Star-schema NL2SQL layer for KPCL Generation Management System (GMS). Query gms_mart.* only; it is a thin view layer over the normalized gms schema. Every fact table states its grain in its comment -- read that before writing GROUP BY.

dim_billing_group.comment: One row per line item on the ESCOM energy bill, e.g. "Sharavathy Valley Project (SVP)", "RTPS Unit 1 & 2". bill_section is HYDEL_RES or THERMAL, matching the two halves of the bill.

dim_btf_location.comment: Boiler tube failure location, e.g. WATER_WALL, RE_HEATER, SUPER_HEATER.

dim_btf_type.comment: Boiler tube failure root cause, e.g. EROSION_SOOT_BLOWER, WELD_DEFECT.

dim_coal_supplier.comment: Coal supplier: MCL, SCCL, WCL (all domestic) or IMPORTED.

dim_counterparty.comment: ESCOMs and other billing counterparties: BESCOM, MESCOM, CESCOM, HESCOM, GESCOM, KPTCL, NTPC, SECI, GoK.

dim_date.comment: One row per calendar day, 01-Apr-2015 onward. Join any fact's date_key here for fy (Apr-Mar financial year, "2024-25"), water_year (Jun-May hydro year), month_label ("MAR-2025"), fy_quarter (Q1-Q4) and season (SUMMER/MONSOON/POST_MONSOON/WINTER). Always group by fy or month_label here rather than by extract(year from date).

dim_outage_reason.comment: Two families of reason code sharing one lookup: reason_class = OUTAGE (why a unit tripped/was shut down; used by fact_unit_outage) or BACKDOWN (why running generation was curtailed; used by fact_generation_loss_daily). Do not mix the two families in one WHERE reason_code = ... across both facts.

dim_reservoir.comment: One row per dam/reservoir (6 rows). feeds_stations lists the hydro stations it supplies, comma separated.

dim_station.comment: One row per power station (33 rows). plant_category_label matches the HO dashboard groups exactly: THERMAL-COAL, MAJOR HYDRO, MINOR HYDRO, GAS, RES (waste-to-energy), SOLAR, WIND. Use plant_category_label for "by category" questions, plant_type_label for the coarser THERMAL/HYDRO/GAS/WTE/SOLAR/WIND split.

dim_unit.comment: One row per generating unit (103 rows), pre-joined to its station's name, company, category and type. unit_id is the natural key used everywhere else, e.g. RTPS-U8. Prefer this over joining unit->station yourself.

fact_coal_receipt.comment: GRAIN: one row per rake delivery (22,300 rows). For a weighted-average GCV over many receipts use SUM(gcv_received_kcal_kg*quantity_mt)/SUM(quantity_mt), never AVG(gcv_received_kcal_kg).

fact_coal_stock_daily.comment: GRAIN: one row per coal station per day (RTPS, BTPS, YTPS). closing_stock_mt = opening + receipt - consumed. "Below norm" = days_of_stock < normative_days.

fact_commercial_transaction.comment: GRAIN: one row per transaction. txn_type_code: ESCOM_BILL_CLAIM, ESCOM_BILL_WITHDRAWAL, RECEIPT, RE_SUBSIDY_GOK, SECI_RECEIPT.

fact_defect.comment: GRAIN: one row per logged defect (DMS). age_or_open_hrs is hours-to-close, or hours-still-open if not yet closed.

fact_energy_bill_escom.comment: GRAIN: one row per ESCOM per billing-group line per bill ("Bill for Sale of Energy to ESCOMs"). amount_rs is that ESCOM's share of that line; SUM(amount_rs) grouped by counterparty_key gives the per-ESCOM total on the bill. line_total_amount_rs repeats the line's grand total (do not SUM it across ESCOM rows).

fact_generation_loss_daily.comment: GRAIN: one row per unit per day per back-down reason (185,988 rows). "Reasons for back-down generation" from the daily report — MU of generation foregone, only for thermal/gas stations (RTPS, BTPS, YTPS, YCCPP). reason_code joins dim_outage_reason WHERE reason_class = 'BACKDOWN'. NO_LOAD_DEMAND rows are also the source of deemed_gen_mu (NLD) in fact_unit_generation_daily.

fact_generation_target_monthly.comment: GRAIN: one row per unit per month (date_key = first day of month). Join dim_date on date_key for fy/month_label. kerc_approved_mu is NULL in almost every row (not yet approved) — do not filter on it being non-null unless asked.

fact_grid_daily.comment: GRAIN: one row per day, Karnataka state grid totals entered at Head Office. KPCL share of state demand = SUM(fact_unit_generation_daily.gross_gen_mu) / SUM(state_consumption_mu) for the same dates.

fact_jmr_meter_monthly.comment: GRAIN: one row per meter per station per month (the signed Joint Meter Reading / Annexure-I). meter_role is UNIT_GEN, UNIT_AUX, COMMON_AUX or STATION_EXPORT. station_net_export_jmr_mu repeats the one billing figure for the whole statement (safe to SUM DISTINCT per station-month, not per row). Compare against fact_unit_generation_daily summed over the month to reconcile billing vs operational energy.

fact_reservoir_daily.comment: GRAIN: one row per dam per day. water_level is in dim_reservoir.level_unit (FT or M) for that reservoir.

fact_station_common_consumption_daily.comment: GRAIN: one row per station per day. Station-level (not unit-level) auxiliary/colony/feeder consumption. True station net export = SUM(unit net_export_mu from fact_unit_generation_daily) - common_aux_mu. Most stations have no row here on most days (common_aux defaults to 0) — LEFT JOIN and COALESCE to 0.

fact_station_generation_daily.comment: GRAIN: one row per station per day — pre-summed from fact_unit_generation_daily so station-level questions need no GROUP BY unit. PLF% = gross_gen_mu/capacity_mu*100; PAF% = declared_capacity_mu/capacity_mu*100.

fact_station_generation_fy.comment: GRAIN: one row per station per financial year (Apr-Mar). PLF% = gross_gen_mu/capacity_mu*100. Use for "this FY vs last FY" and "top N stations by annual generation" questions.

fact_station_generation_monthly.comment: GRAIN: one row per station per month (the Monthly Performance Report, station columns). date_key = first of month.

fact_unit_cumulative.comment: GRAIN: one row per unit, cumulative generation/hours/trips since first synchronisation (opening balance + everything in fact_unit_generation_daily since). "Life-to-date" questions.

fact_unit_current_status.comment: GRAIN: one row per unit, always "right now" (no date_key — this is not history). status is RUNNING, FORCED_OUTAGE, PLANNED_OUTAGE, RSD_OUTAGE or DECOMMISSIONED. Use for "which units are down right now" questions.

fact_unit_generation_daily.comment: GRAIN: one row per unit per calendar day (365,132 rows). The base fact for every generation/PLF/fuel question. Join dim_date on date_key and dim_unit on unit_key to slice by fy/month/season/station/category. Ratios are NOT stored here: compute PLF as SUM(gross_gen_mu)/SUM(capacity_mu)*100, aux% as SUM(aux_consumption_mu)/SUM(gross_gen_mu)*100, specific coal as SUM(coal_consumed_mt)/1000/SUM(gross_gen_mu) -- always SUM/SUM over the rows in scope, never AVG a per-row ratio. For a station total, SUM over its units; station net export additionally subtracts common-aux — see fact_station_common_consumption_daily.

fact_unit_outage.comment: GRAIN: one row per trip/shutdown event (5,877 rows). outage_type is FORCED, PLANNED or RSD. is_open = true means the unit is still out (sync_at is NULL); outage_hrs is then computed live to now. is_btf = true for boiler tube failures, with btf_type_key/btf_location_key filled from the DMS register. For "currently down" questions, filter is_open = true directly rather than re-deriving status per unit.

metrics.name: PLF
metrics.label: Plant Load Factor %
metrics.notes: capacity_mu = capacity_mw * hours_in_period / 1000. Never AVG a per-row percentage.

metrics.name: aux_pct
metrics.label: Auxiliary consumption %
metrics.notes: For station-level aux %, add common_aux_mu from fact_station_common_consumption_daily to the numerator.

metrics.name: weighted_avg_gcv_coal
metrics.label: Weighted-average coal GCV, kcal/kg
metrics.notes: Also used for coal receipts: SUM(gcv_received_kcal_kg*quantity_mt)/SUM(quantity_mt) on fact_coal_receipt.

metrics.name: net_export_station
metrics.label: Station net export, MU
metrics.formula: SUM(unit gross_gen_mu) - SUM(unit aux_consumption_mu) - station common_aux_mu
metrics.notes: Already computed as net_export_mu in fact_station_generation_daily/monthly/fy.

metrics.name: coal_stock_below_norm_days
metrics.label: Days a station's coal cover fell below the normative level

metrics.name: kpcl_share_of_state_demand
metrics.label: KPCL share of Karnataka state consumption, %

metrics.name: backdown_loss_by_reason
metrics.label: Generation lost to back-down, by reason

metrics.name: yoy_growth_pct
metrics.label: Year-on-year growth %
metrics.notes: Self-join fact_station_generation_fy on station_key where fy differs by one.

synonyms.MU: million kWh, the standard energy unit used throughout
synonyms.NLD: deemed generation lost to no-load-demand back-down; column deemed_gen_mu
synonyms.back-down / backdown: generation curtailed below capability; fact_generation_loss_daily, reason_class=BACKDOWN in dim_outage_reason
synonyms.trip: a FORCED outage event; fact_unit_outage where outage_type='FORCED'
synonyms.RSD: Reserve Shut Down -- unit available but not required; rsd_hrs / outage_type='RSD'
synonyms.BTF / BTL: Boiler Tube Failure / Leak; fact_unit_outage where is_btf=true, joined to dim_btf_type / dim_btf_location
synonyms.JMR: Joint Meter Reading, the monthly signed billing statement; fact_jmr_meter_monthly
synonyms.MPR: Monthly Performance Report; fact_station_generation_monthly / fact_unit_generation (aggregate to month)
synonyms.RES: Renewable Energy Source station on the dashboard = waste-to-energy (BWTEP) in this data
synonyms.CEA target: generation_target.cea_target_mu, the Central Electricity Authority monthly target
synonyms.declared capacity / DC: declared_capacity_mu, the day's declared availability; drives PAF
synonyms.ESCOM: electricity distribution company: BESCOM, MESCOM, CESCOM, HESCOM, GESCOM -- dim_counterparty

join_rules: Every fact table has a date_key -> join gms_mart.dim_date for fy / month_label / season / water_year.
Every fact table has a unit_key or station_key (never both required) -> join dim_unit or dim_station for names/category.
Do not join gms_mart views back to gms.* tables directly; gms_mart already carries every attribute you need.
fact_unit_outage.reason_code joins dim_outage_reason WHERE reason_class='OUTAGE'; fact_generation_loss_daily.reason_code joins WHERE reason_class='BACKDOWN'. Do not cross the two.

examples.question: What was KPCL's gross generation and net export in FY 2024-25 by plant category?
Which stations generated less than their CEA target in March 2025?
examples.sql:
SELECT s.station_name, round(f.gross_gen_mu, 3) AS actual_mu, f.cea_target_mu,
       round(f.gross_gen_mu - f.cea_target_mu, 3) AS shortfall_mu
FROM fact_station_generation_monthly f JOIN dim_date d USING (date_key) JOIN dim_station s USING (station_key)
WHERE d.month_label = 'MAR-2025' AND f.gross_gen_mu < f.cea_target_mu ORDER BY shortfall_mu;

examples.question: FY 2024-25 generation vs last FY for each station
examples.sql:
SELECT cur.station_key, cur.gross_gen_mu AS fy_2024_25, prev.gross_gen_mu AS fy_2023_24,
       round((cur.gross_gen_mu / NULLIF(prev.gross_gen_mu, 0) - 1) * 100, 2) AS yoy_pct
FROM fact_station_generation_fy cur LEFT JOIN fact_station_generation_fy prev
       ON prev.station_key = cur.station_key AND prev.fy = '2023-24'
WHERE cur.fy = '2024-25' ORDER BY cur.gross_gen_mu DESC;

examples.question: SGS generation in water year 2024-25 vs water year 2023-24
Unit-wise generation, peak load, PLF, running hours and trips at RTPS on 06-Apr-2025
examples.sql:
SELECT u.unit_id, f.gross_gen_mu, f.peak_load_mw, round(f.gross_gen_mu / f.capacity_mu * 100, 2) AS plf_pct,
       f.running_hrs, f.forced_outage_hrs, f.trips
FROM fact_unit_generation_daily f JOIN dim_unit u USING (unit_key)
WHERE f.station_key = 'RTPS' AND f.date_key = '2025-04-06' ORDER BY u.unit_no;

examples.question: What is the highest single-day generation of RTPS ever, and in FY 2024-25?
examples.sql:
SELECT 'ever' AS scope, date_key, gross_gen_mu FROM
  (SELECT date_key, gross_gen_mu FROM fact_station_generation_daily WHERE station_key = 'RTPS' ORDER BY gross_gen_mu DESC LIMIT 1) a
UNION ALL
SELECT 'FY 2024-25', f.date_key, f.gross_gen_mu FROM fact_station_generation_daily f JOIN dim_date d USING (date_key)
WHERE f.station_key = 'RTPS' AND d.fy = '2024-25' ORDER BY gross_gen_mu DESC LIMIT 1;

examples.question: RTPS unit-wise MPR for March 2025 (generation, PLF, PAF, aux %, specific coal, specific oil, GCV, heat rate)
examples.sql:
SELECT u.unit_id, round(sum(f.gross_gen_mu), 3) gross_gen_mu,
       round(sum(f.gross_gen_mu) / sum(f.capacity_mu) * 100, 2) AS plf_pct,
       round(sum(f.declared_capacity_mu) / sum(f.capacity_mu) * 100, 2) AS paf_pct,
       round(sum(f.aux_consumption_mu) / NULLIF(sum(f.gross_gen_mu), 0) * 100, 2) AS aux_pct,
       round(sum(f.coal_consumed_mt) / 1000 / NULLIF(sum(f.gross_gen_mu), 0), 3) AS sp_coal_kg_kwh,
       round(sum(f.hfo_consumed_kl + f.ldo_consumed_kl) / NULLIF(sum(f.gross_gen_mu), 0), 3) AS sp_oil_ml_kwh,
       round(sum(f.gcv_coal_kcal_kg * f.coal_consumed_mt) / NULLIF(sum(f.coal_consumed_mt) FILTER (WHERE f.gcv_coal_kcal_kg IS NOT NULL), 0)) AS wa_gcv_kcal_kg,
       round(sum(f.gross_heat_rate_kcal_kwh * f.gross_gen_mu) / NULLIF(sum(f.gross_gen_mu) FILTER (WHERE f.gross_heat_rate_kcal_kwh IS NOT NULL), 0)) AS wa_heat_rate_kcal_kwh,
       max(f.gross_gen_mu) AS max_day_gen_mu
FROM fact_unit_generation_daily f JOIN dim_date d USING (date_key) JOIN dim_unit u USING (unit_key)
WHERE f.station_key = 'RTPS' AND d.month_label = 'MAR-2025' GROUP BY u.unit_id, u.unit_no ORDER BY u.unit_no;

examples.question: RTPS station totals for FY 2024-25 and March 2025 (check against the source MPR: 8310.351 and 831.212 MU)
examples.sql:
SELECT 'FY 2024-25' AS period, round(gross_gen_mu, 3) FROM fact_station_generation_fy WHERE station_key = 'RTPS' AND fy = '2024-25'
UNION ALL
SELECT 'MAR-2025', round(f.gross_gen_mu, 3) FROM fact_station_generation_monthly f JOIN dim_date d USING (date_key)
WHERE f.station_key = 'RTPS' AND d.month_label = 'MAR-2025';

examples.question: Actual gross heat rate vs design heat rate per BTPS unit in FY 2024-25
examples.sql:
SELECT u.unit_id, u.design_heat_rate_kcal_kwh,
       round(sum(f.gross_heat_rate_kcal_kwh * f.gross_gen_mu) / sum(f.gross_gen_mu)) AS actual_ghr
FROM fact_unit_generation_daily f JOIN dim_date d USING (date_key) JOIN dim_unit u USING (unit_key)
WHERE f.station_key = 'BTPS' AND d.fy = '2024-25' AND f.gross_gen_mu > 0
GROUP BY u.unit_id, u.design_heat_rate_kcal_kwh ORDER BY u.unit_id;

examples.question: Cumulative generation, running hours and trips since first synchronisation for RTPS units
examples.sql:
SELECT unit_key, round(cum_gen_mu, 3) cum_gen_mu, cum_running_hrs, cum_trips, as_on_date
FROM fact_unit_cumulative WHERE station_key = 'RTPS' ORDER BY unit_key;

examples.question: RTPS back-down in FY 2024-25 by reason
examples.sql:
SELECT r.description, round(sum(f.loss_mu), 3) AS loss_mu
FROM fact_generation_loss_daily f JOIN dim_date d USING (date_key) JOIN dim_outage_reason r ON r.reason_key = f.reason_code
WHERE f.station_key = 'RTPS' AND d.fy = '2024-25' AND r.reason_class = 'BACKDOWN'
GROUP BY r.description ORDER BY loss_mu DESC;

examples.question: Number of forced outages and outage hours by reason at BTPS in FY 2023-24
examples.sql:
SELECT r.description, count(*) AS outages, round(sum(f.outage_hrs), 2) AS outage_hrs
FROM fact_unit_outage f JOIN dim_date d USING (date_key) JOIN dim_outage_reason r ON r.reason_key = f.reason_code
WHERE f.station_key = 'BTPS' AND d.fy = '2023-24' AND f.outage_type = 'FORCED' AND r.reason_class = 'OUTAGE'
GROUP BY r.description ORDER BY outages DESC;

examples.question: List boiler tube failures of BTPS-U3 in January 2024 with failure type and location
examples.sql:
SELECT f.outage_key, f.trip_at, f.sync_at, f.outage_hrs, t.description AS failure_type, l.description AS location
FROM fact_unit_outage f JOIN dim_date d USING (date_key)
JOIN dim_btf_type t ON t.btf_type_key = f.btf_type_key JOIN dim_btf_location l ON l.btf_location_key = f.btf_location_key
WHERE f.unit_key = 'BTPS-U3' AND f.is_btf AND d.month_start = '2024-01-01' ORDER BY f.trip_at;

examples.question: Which boiler tube failure location is most common across all thermal stations?
Which units are currently not running, and since when?
examples.sql: SELECT unit_key, status, status_since, reason_code FROM fact_unit_current_status WHERE status <> 'RUNNING' ORDER BY status_since;

examples.question: On how many days in FY 2024-25 was each station's coal stock below normative days?
Rakes, quantity and weighted GCV of coal received by supplier in FY 2024-25
examples.sql:
SELECT f.supplier_code, sum(f.no_of_rakes) rakes, round(sum(f.quantity_mt)) quantity_mt,
       round(sum(f.gcv_received_kcal_kg * f.quantity_mt) / sum(f.quantity_mt)) AS wa_gcv_kcal_kg
FROM fact_coal_receipt f JOIN dim_date d USING (date_key)
WHERE d.fy = '2024-25' GROUP BY f.supplier_code ORDER BY quantity_mt DESC;

examples.question: RTPS coal position on 06-Apr-2025 (OB, receipt, consumption, CB)
examples.sql:
SELECT opening_stock_mt, receipt_mt, indigenous_consumed_mt, imported_consumed_mt, total_consumed_mt, closing_stock_mt, days_of_stock
FROM fact_coal_stock_daily WHERE station_key = 'RTPS' AND date_key = '2025-04-06';

examples.question: Linganamakki level, storage % and energy on 06-Apr-2025 vs the same day last year
examples.sql:
SELECT date_key, water_level, capacity_pct, energy_potential_mu
FROM fact_reservoir_daily WHERE reservoir_key = 1 AND date_key IN ('2025-04-06', '2024-04-06');

examples.question: Which power stations are fed by Supa dam, and what did they generate in water year 2024-25?
examples.sql:
SELECT s.station_key, round(sum(f.gross_gen_mu), 3) AS gross_gen_mu
FROM dim_reservoir r
JOIN fact_station_generation_daily f ON f.station_key = ANY (string_to_array(r.feeds_stations, ', '))
JOIN dim_date d USING (date_key) JOIN dim_station s USING (station_key)
WHERE r.reservoir_name = 'SUPA' AND d.water_year = '2024-25' GROUP BY s.station_key;

examples.question: KPCL share of state consumption in March 2025
examples.sql:
SELECT round(sum(k.gross_gen_mu) / sum(g.state_consumption_mu) * 100, 2) AS kpcl_share_pct
FROM fact_grid_daily g JOIN dim_date d ON d.date_key = g.date_key
JOIN (SELECT date_key, sum(gross_gen_mu) gross_gen_mu FROM fact_station_generation_daily GROUP BY date_key) k ON k.date_key = g.date_key
WHERE d.month_label = 'MAR-2025';

examples.question: SGS generation by season in FY 2023-24
Quarter-wise PLF of thermal stations in FY 2024-25
examples.sql:
SELECT f.station_key, d.fy_quarter, round(sum(f.gross_gen_mu) / sum(f.capacity_mu) * 100, 2) AS plf_pct
FROM fact_station_generation_daily f JOIN dim_date d USING (date_key) JOIN dim_station s USING (station_key)
WHERE s.plant_category_label = 'THERMAL-COAL' AND d.fy = '2024-25'
GROUP BY f.station_key, d.fy_quarter ORDER BY f.station_key, d.fy_quarter;

examples.question: Weekday vs weekend average daily KPCL generation in FY 2024-25
